metadata.title: The Outvoting Problem
metadata.audience: Students and practitioners learning to use and report on AI systems
metadata.fellow: Janvi Chitroda, AI Data Engineer volunteer, Medhavy project, Humanitarians AI
metadata.source: inbox/term2-week08/term2-week8-video-content.md (Week 8); narration supplied verbatim and pre-approved by Janvi (2026-10-27)
metadata.note: STEM/learning film, hai Plain register on the ai-explainer chassis. Thesis: majority vote counts every judge the same, so two weaker judges that agree can outvote a much stronger one — correlated errors line up instead of cancelling; options exist (weighting, a strong judge's veto to review, unanimity) but are untested, and weighting needs measured skill first. Worked example: Week 8 three-judge sensitivity test (98% · 68.7% · 64.0% alone, ensemble 74.0%, outvoted in 36 of 39 misses). On-screen data numbers appear in the Week 8 source (69 = 68.7 rounded as the narration rounds); the Your Turn size (20) is Janvi's supplied task.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude composer, ask lands answered. Required intro line + AI-narration disclosure.
beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Janvi and this video is about a weakness of majority voting: a strong judge can be outvoted by two weaker ones that agree. This narration is an AI-generated voice; the work is mine.

props.command: My strongest AI judge flags an item, but the other two say ship. Under majority vote, who wins?
output: Count how often your strong judge is overruled
Measure each judge on known errors

beats.role_note: Three equal ballot boxes; caption 'every vote counts the same'; one judge marked 'much better at the task'.
beats.narration_text: Majority vote treats every judge equally. That's fair when judges are similar. It's a problem when one judge is much better at the task.
beats.visual_intent: Three equal ballot boxes; caption 'every vote counts the same'; one judge marked 'much better at the task'.

beats.narration_text: In our planted-error test, one judge caught 98 percent of errors, and the other two caught 69 and 64. Yet the ensemble caught 74.

beats.role_note: Vote card 2 'ship' vs 1 'flag' → ship; counter '36 of 39 misses'.
beats.narration_text: Because when the two weaker judges agree on the same wrong answer, they win two to one. That happened in 36 of our 39 misses.
beats.visual_intent: Vote card 2 'ship' vs 1 'flag' → ship; counter '36 of 39 misses'.

beats.role_note: Two weaker judges' miss sets overlapping heavily (Venn), strong judge mostly outside.
beats.narration_text: This is where correlated errors bite. The two weaker judges passed the same corrupted items together, so their mistakes lined up instead of cancelling out.
beats.visual_intent: Two weaker judges' miss sets overlapping heavily (Venn), strong judge mostly outside.

beats.role_note: Three option cards marked 'not yet tested': weight by measured skill · one strong judge can send to review · ship only if all agree; trade-off arrow 'fewer errors shipped ↔ more human review'.
beats.narration_text: Options worth testing: weight judges by measured performance, let a strong judge send an item to review on its own, or ship only when all judges agree. Each trades more human review for fewer errors shipped. We haven't tested these yet.
beats.visual_intent: Three option cards marked 'not yet tested': weight by measured skill · one strong judge can send to review · ship only if all agree; trade-off arrow 'fewer errors shipped ↔ more human review'.

show.event: fewer errors shipped ↔ more human review

beats.role_note: Card 'can't measure who is stronger? weighting = another assumption'; arrow 'measure first, on known errors'.
beats.narration_text: When not to change the vote: if you can't measure which judge is stronger on your task, weighting just swaps one assumption for another. Measure first, on known errors.
beats.visual_intent: Card 'can't measure who is stronger? weighting = another assumption'; arrow 'measure first, on known errors'.

show.event: when not to change the vote

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in the composer.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. For your own ensemble, find items where the majority overruled one judge, and check a sample by hand to see who was right.

props.command: Find items where the majority overruled one judge, and pick 20 for me to check by hand.
